title: TradingViewBuilder: readable trading rules in Pine Script

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Moving averages, RSI, Bollinger Bands: what do those classic trading rules look like as actual code?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'd guess a lot of them are buried in long scripts.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: This repository goes the other way. It's a collection of TradingView indicators and strategies in Pine Script, one file per technique, small enough to read in a sitting. It's an AlgoÉTS project.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What's the difference between an indicator and a strategy?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: An indicator just plots values on the chart. A strategy adds entry orders. For example, the RSI strategy goes long when the fourteen-period RSI crosses above thirty, and short when it crosses below seventy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nothing to install. Paste a file into the Pine Editor in TradingView, add it to the chart, and change lengths and levels from the gear icon to compare the trades.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Eight classic techniques are covered, plus a draft of a time-series momentum idea across sixty futures contracts.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The written page lists each technique and rule.
